title: Sell Mineral Rights in McMechen, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McMechen, WV
metaDescription: McMechen, Marshall County mineral owners: dense Marcellus/Utica units near Moundsville, stacked-pay pooling, and multi-generation heir splits.
heroLead: McMechen sits in Marshall County's dense Marcellus and Utica corridor, where large pooled units and stacked-pay development both touch nearby acreage.
intro: As one of the smaller Ohio River communities in core Marshall County, McMechen's surrounding tracts have been drawn into some of the larger horizontal spacing units operators have assembled in this part of the state, often combining formations at different depths under a single pad.

sections.heading: Stacked-pay units near the Ohio River
paragraphs: Marshall County's geology supports both Marcellus and deeper Utica/Point Pleasant development, and McMechen-area acreage sits close enough to active pads that stacked-pay units are a real possibility for some tracts. Confirming whether your interest is developed for one formation or two changes how many separate royalty streams you should expect.

sections.heading: Pooled acreage and older farm-tract boundaries
paragraphs: Horizontal units in this part of Marshall County frequently combine several original farm tracts, some of which predate the town's incorporation. Your pro-rata royalty share depends on your original tract's surface acreage relative to the full unit, which should be confirmed against the actual filed unit plat rather than assumed.

sections.heading: Why McMechen's small footprint doesn't mean a small interest
paragraphs: McMechen is one of Marshall County's smaller communities by land area, but that doesn't correlate with the size of a mineral interest tied to a given tract — value depends on unit participation, formation, and lease terms, not on how large the town itself is. Some of the county's more valuable fractional interests sit under modest residential lots here rather than large rural farms.
If you've assumed your McMechen-area interest is too small to be worth pursuing, a quick records check against current unit filings is worth doing before ruling it out.

faqs.question: Could my McMechen interest be under both the Marcellus and the Utica?
faqs.answer: It's possible given the county's stacked-pay geology. Checking your division orders and unit filings against both formations will confirm whether you have one or two royalty streams.

faqs.question: How is my share of a large pooled McMechen-area unit calculated?
faqs.answer: As your original tract's surface acreage divided by the unit's total acreage, applied against your royalty percentage. The filed unit plat has the exact figures.

faqs.question: My family's tract near McMechen has multiple heirs — how do we sell?
faqs.answer: Each heir can sell their own documented fractional share individually; a full family consensus isn't required for an individual sale.

faqs.question: Is a small residential-lot mineral interest in McMechen worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: It can be — lot size doesn't determine interest value, unit participation and lease terms do.
